newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity front months steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity front months steady to lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures front months were trading steady to lower Friday, retrenching after a significant drop in morning trade ahead of expiry of the December contracts.
Sources said electricity may have been sent on a rollercoaster ride by higher natural gas futures and reports of some lower western physicals prices.
"It is still bouncing around a little bit with gas, but (December California Oregon Border futures) seem to be coming back a bit now to where they should be," said one futures broker.
Natural gas prices rose sharply this week, with NYMEX December Henry Hub gas hitting an all time high of $4.00 per million British thermal units on Thursday just ahead of the contract expiry.
Friday is the final day of trade for the December electricity futures.
As of 1230 EDT, December California Oregon Border (COB) was trading steady from Thursday's settle at $28.00 after trade as low as $27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
January COB was trading down 73 cents at $23.90 after trade as high as $25.00 and as low as $23.50 per MWh.
December Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 16 cents at $27.75 after exchanges as low as $26.75, while January was down $1.00 at $23.00 per MWh.
February PV had traded up 15 cents at $21.00 per MWh.
Contract volumes for Friday were not available.
